basics.name: Romeo Silvestri
basics.label: ML Engineer
basics.summary: Machine Learning Engineer with 3+ years of professional and research experience, combining a strong foundation in statistics and data science with applied machine learning and AI research. Experienced in developing end-to-end ML systems across forecasting, reinforcement learning, and generative AI, from scientific experimentation and validation to MLOps and production deployment. Author of peer-reviewed publications, with a focus on translating research into robust, data-driven systems with real-world applications.

work.name: Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK)
work.summary: FBK is a leading Italian research institute focused on science and technology innovation, with a strong emphasis on AI, data science, and their real-world applications across sectors including agriculture, health, and industry.
highlights: Designed, tested, and deployed a Decision Support System for water management, integrating heterogeneous data sources, including IoT sensors and weather data, reducing operational costs by around 50% across several companies.

Operationalized research prototypes through reproducible ML pipelines and APIs using Python, FastAPI, MLflow, and GitLab, supporting experimentation and production deployment in collaboration with domain experts.
Developed a PPO-based Deep Reinforcement Learning agent in a digital-twin environment combining surrogate and physics-based models for simulation and policy training.

Developed WeatherSynth, a modular Python library for composing and benchmarking reproducible synthetic weather-generation pipelines with interchangeable generators, climate conditioners, physical constraints, and diagnostics.

Developed a multi-agent LLM/RAG assistant using LangChain and LangGraph, integrating technical and regulatory knowledge for real-time agricultural decision support with global and region-specific recommendations.
Built and evaluated ARIMA, XGBoost, and LSTM models for sensor time-series forecasting, achieving low prediction error through feature engineering, hyperparameter tuning, and rigorous validation.
Developed and benchmarked a Wasserstein-based drift detector for online regression monitoring, comparing it with established methods and evaluating its applicability to sensor forecasting.
Evaluated IoT soil-sensor behavior and anomaly-detection methods in collaboration with industry and academic partners to assess sensor quality, reliability, and suitability for practical field use.

work.name: Youbidata
work.summary: Youbidata is a data-driven startup specializing in business intelligence and advanced analytics, helping companies make informed decisions through customized data solutions and strategic consulting.
highlights: Developed a centralized financial monitoring dashboard using PostgreSQL and Power BI to consolidate, track, and visualize key financial KPIs, supporting reporting and decision-making for a consulting client.

work.name: Italian National Institute of Statistics (ISTAT)
work.summary: ISTAT is the official statistical agency of Italy, responsible for collecting, analyzing, and disseminating data to support government planning, public policy, and socio-economic research.
highlights: Analyzed national demographic data using R and SQL to uncover socio-economic trends and produce periodic reports.
Evaluated the Austrian quality framework's suitability for the Italian Census, achieving statistically significant results.

work.name: Sapienza University of Rome
highlights: Supported the study of statistics-related subjects and managed IT services.
